title: Rapid Evaluation of Chaboche–Voce Material Model Parameters Through a Fully Reversed Strain-Controlled Test
content: Modeling cyclic plasticity remains challenging due to the high computational cost of nonlinear constitutive models and the large number of parameters requiring evaluation, which are often temperature-dependent. This work presents a systematic procedure for identifying the parameters of the Chaboche–Voce model, one of the most widely adopted constitutive models for cyclic plasticity and commonly implemented in finite element software. Due to its nonlinear formulation, however, parameter evaluation is not straightforward. The parameters governing the kinematic hardening response are determined through a simple least-squares fit, yielding an analytical expression for a branch of the mid-life stabilized cycle. The Voce parameters are subsequently obtained by solving an analytical equation followed by a further least-squares fit. The resulting methodology provides a systematic approach for characterizing materials exhibiting both cyclic hardening and softening. The procedure was applied to two materials: 42CrMo4+QT tested at room temperature at different strain ranges for two different values of mean strain and 1Cr-1Mo-0.25V steel tested at different temperatures and strain ranges. The proposed approach provides satisfactory constitutive parameters while requiring virtually negligible computational cost, making it suitable for efficient material characterization and subsequent finite element implementation.
